title: Configuration tables
summary: Drive a hex nut from a spreadsheet's configuration table, and switch it from M10 to M12.

credit.changes: Words in Simplified Technical English, FreeCAD 1.1 names. The body comes first, the spreadsheet after the pad. The steps with a SubShapeBinder or a Link (variant links) are left out: the configuration changes on the body itself. The column WidthAcrossCorners has the name Width. Each check reads the expressions and the volume of the nut.

steps.say: Push **{PartDesign_NewSketch|Create sketch}**. Select the XY plane. Push **OK**. Give the sketch the label **Profile**.
steps.why: The expressions later find the sketch by this label.
hints: Find the sketch button in the Part Design toolbar.
Push **F2** on the sketch in the tree to change its label.
Plane: XY, label: Profile.

steps.say: Draw a hexagon on the origin. Draw a circle on the origin, inside the hexagon. Push **Close**.
steps.why: The hexagon is the outside of the nut; the circle is its hole.

picture.alt: A hexagon and a circle, both on the origin, with no dimensions yet.

hints: Put the centre of each on the origin point.
Use the hexagon tool and the circle tool of the Sketcher.
A hexagon of six lines and one circle, both centred on the origin.

steps.say: Push **{PartDesign_Pad|Pad}**. Keep the default length. Push **OK**.
steps.why: The spreadsheet sets the thickness later.
hints: Find Pad in the Part Design toolbar.
Any length is good for now.
Pad with its default length, OK.

steps.say: Push **{Spreadsheet_CreateSheet|Create spreadsheet}**. Type the table of the picture. Open the context menu of cell **A2**. Select **Configuration table…**. Push **OK**.
steps.why: The second row shows the values of the configuration in use.
steps.explain: The first row holds the titles: Variant, Diameter, Width, Thickness. Keep the second row empty. The third row holds **M10**: 10 mm, 18.48 mm, 8.4 mm. The fourth row holds **M12**: 12 mm, 20.78 mm, 10.8 mm. Width is the width across the corners. In the Setup Configuration Table dialog, set the cell range **A2** to **D4** and the property **Nut.Configuration**. Give each cell of the second row the alias of its column title.

picture.alt: A spreadsheet: titles in the first row, the values in use below them, and a row for each nut size.

hints: Leave the second row empty: the configuration table fills it.
In the dialog, set the cell range and the property of the body.
Range **A2** to **D4**, property **Nut.Configuration**. Aliases on the second row: **Diameter**, **Width** and **Thickness**.

steps.say: Open **Profile**. Give the circle a diameter. Type **=Spreadsheet.Diameter** as its value. Give the corners of the hexagon a diameter from **Width**.
steps.why: The sketch now takes its sizes from the spreadsheet.

picture.alt: The nut sketch with two diameters: the hole and the corners of the hexagon.

hints: Type an equals sign in the value box to start an expression.
Bind the circle and the construction circle of the hexagon.
**=Spreadsheet.Diameter** and **=Spreadsheet.Width**.
Find Length in the Property view of the pad.
Type an equals sign to start an expression.
Length = **=Spreadsheet.Thickness**.

steps.say: Select **Nut** in the tree. Set its **Configuration** to **M12**.
steps.why: One switch changes all three sizes of the nut.
hints: Configuration is a property of the body.
Open the list of the Configuration property.
Configuration = **M12**.

steps.say: Done: a hex nut that changes size through its configuration table.
